feature: A group you opened in the layers list is still open when you come back
summary: Which groups a picture has open in its layers list is now remembered per file, so reopening a picture shows the same rows you left rather than every group shut. Opening a group is still not an edit: it costs no undo step and the file on disk is untouched.
setup: Photonz Dev, Experiments window, release Next, with layer groups on. Nothing new to turn on.

try.do: Open a screenshot, draw two rectangles on it, select both and press Command G.
Double click one of the rectangles on the canvas so the layers list opens the group.
Save the picture, then close the window.
Quit Photonz and start it again.
Open the same file and look at the layers list without clicking anything.
Shut the group, close the window, reopen the file: it should be shut.
Press Command Z and confirm undo has nothing to do with any of this.

evaluate: Coming back to a picture with the same groups open, is that what you expected, or did you want a clean shut list every time?
With a deep tree, does reopening everything you had open feel like picking up where you left off, or like a wall of rows?
A picture you have never saved is not remembered, because there is no file to remember it against. Does that ever bite you?
Should shutting every group and reopening the file bring back nothing, as it does now, or should the app have a view of its own?
rough: Two windows on the same file share one record, so the last one to open or shut a group is the one remembered. Nobody has hit this; say so if you do.
A never-saved picture is not remembered at all. The alternative is remembering it against a window that will not exist next launch, which is worse.
The record is capped at the last 60 files, oldest first, so it cannot grow without end. A file you have not touched in a long while opens shut.
The screenshots are real screen captures of the probe app, taken with the Screen Recording grant, not offscreen renders.
